title: Write every slide in English, for a studio owner doing repeat maintenance work who is paid job-by-job and feels every quiet week.

brief.idea:
Write every slide in English, for a studio owner doing repeat maintenance work who is paid job-by-job and feels every quiet week.

THIS DECK IS ADVICE, NOT A PITCH. Someone who saves it should be able to build their first package from these slides alone. Every slide must carry something actionable in its BODY — a decision, a rule, a concrete example. A slide that is only a headline and a mood is a wasted slide.

The material, which is all you may assert:

- Paid job by job, income is the exact shape of the calendar. The problem is not a lack of clients, it is a lack of strategy.
- A package is sessions the client pays for up front. The studio sets the session count, the price, an optional discount and an optional expiry.
- ONE session sells several services together: a full detail plus a ceramic coating. SEVERAL sessions sell the same service repeatedly: five interior details.
- The price must cover every session. On a single-session package, price it so the package beats buying those services separately.
- The discount is the easiest part to get wrong. You are buying commitment, not doing charity. A small discount on a five-session package is enough: the client has already decided to come back five times, and that is worth more than any discount. A large discount turns a loyal client into one who shops on price.
- An expiry on a multi-session package is what makes clients actually come back.
- The client buys and pays online before anything is booked. A package can also be assigned by hand as compensation: no payment to process, recorded either way.
- Each use takes one session off the total, and you always see who holds a package and how many sessions remain.
- An online purchase records three figures: the price paid, the platform's commission, and your net.

Invent no statistics, percentages or facts beyond this. The only numbers available: one session, five sessions, three visits, 5%, one month, three figures.
plan: Cover. The hook: getting paid before you touch the car. Name the quiet week as the problem.
The problem, stated plainly: paid job by job, income is the exact shape of the calendar — a lack of strategy, not a lack of clients.
What a package is: sessions paid for up front, with the studio setting the session count, price, optional discount and optional expiry.

The first decision — HOW MANY SESSIONS. Give both cases with their examples: one session to sell several services together (full detail + ceramic coating); several to sell the same service repeatedly (five interior details).
The second decision — PRICE. It must cover every session; on a single-session package price it so the package beats buying those services separately.
The third decision — DISCOUNT. You are buying commitment, not doing charity. Small is enough on five sessions; a large discount turns a loyal client into one who shops on price. Say to start at 5%.

The fourth decision — EXPIRY, and what you get back: an expiry is what makes clients return; each use takes a session off the total, you always see who holds what, and the purchase records the price paid, the commission and your net.

Close: this week, build a five-session package around your most repeated service, start the discount at 5%, offer it to clients who have returned three times or more, and after a month compare your net against billing job by job. Ask the reader to DM the keyword PACKAGE.

PHOTOGRAPHY: this brand is carried by its images — most slides that show a place, a product, a person or a result should ask for one.
DO: Speak to 'you' and 'your studio'; Short, evocative fragments; Concrete business outcomes (bookings, rebookings, revenue); Let restraint imply premium
DON'T: Exclamation marks; Tech jargon; Overt hype or ALL-CAPS shouting; Generic SaaS clichés
